en: n. a dark shape made on a surface when something blocks the light; an area that is darker than the area around it; a small amount of something; vt. to follow someone secretly; to block light from something
ex: The tree cast a long shadow across the lawn.
那棵樹在草坪上投下長長的影子。

en: n. a person whose job is to look after sheep; a large dog trained to herd sheep; a minister who cares for a group of people; vt. to guide or lead people somewhere carefully
ex: The shepherd led his sheep to the green hills.
牧羊人把羊群帶到青翠的山丘。

en: n. a small sea animal with a hard shell, ten legs and a curved body that is eaten as food; (informal) a very small person; vi. to catch shrimp
ex: We ordered grilled shrimp with garlic butter.
我們點了蒜香奶油烤蝦。

en: vi. to become smaller in size or amount; to move back because you are afraid; vt. to make something smaller; n. (informal) a psychiatrist
ex: My sweater shrank after I washed it in hot water.
我的毛衣用熱水洗過後縮水了。

en: n. a sound, light or movement that gives information or a warning; a radio or TV wave; vt. to make a sign to someone; to show that something is going to happen; vi. to send a sign
ex: The driver gave a signal before turning left.
司機在左轉前打了方向燈。

en: n. the fact of being similar; a way in which two things are alike
ex: There is a strong similarity between the two languages.
這兩種語言有很強的相似性。

en: a. showing what you really think or feel; honest and not pretending; genuine
ex: She gave a sincere apology for her mistake.
她為自己的過錯誠心道歉。

en: n. the set of things that are happening in a particular place or at a particular time; the position that someone is in; the place where something is
ex: The economic situation is getting worse every month.
經濟情勢一個月比一個月糟。

en: n. a boot with a metal blade for moving on ice; a flat sea fish; vi. to move smoothly on ice or on a hard surface using skates; to slide easily over a surface
ex: The children skate on the frozen lake every winter.
孩子們每年冬天都在結冰的湖上滑冰。

en: n. a long narrow piece of wood or plastic used to move over snow; vi. to move over snow wearing skis
ex: We go skiing in the mountains every winter.
我們每年冬天都去山上滑雪。

en: a. very thin, often in an unattractive way; (informal) (of clothes) fitting very closely to the body; (of a drink) made with skim milk
ex: The stray cat was so skinny that I could see its ribs.
那隻流浪貓瘦得看得見肋骨。

en: vi. to jump lightly from one foot to the other; to leave out a part of something; vt. to not do or attend something; n. a light jump; a large container for waste
ex: I skipped breakfast and ate lunch early.
我沒吃早餐，提早吃了午餐。

en: n. a person who is owned by another person and has to work for them without pay; a person who is controlled by something; vi. to work very hard
ex: Many slaves were forced to work in the cotton fields.
許多奴隸被迫在棉花田裡工作。

en: n. the part of a piece of clothing that covers your arm; a flat paper cover for a record; vt. to put sleeves on a garment
ex: She rolled up her sleeves and started to cook.
她捲起袖子開始煮飯。
ph: 捲起袖子，準備大幹一場
wear one's heart on one's sleeve

en: a. gracefully thin; very small in amount; thin and narrow
ex: She has a slender figure and long hair.
她身形苗條，一頭長髮。

en: n. a thin flat piece cut from a larger piece of food; a part or share of something; vt. to cut something into thin flat pieces; vi. to cut through something easily
ex: Would you like a slice of cake?
你想吃一片蛋糕嗎？

en: a. smooth, wet or greasy so that it is difficult to hold or walk on; not honest or trustworthy; difficult to deal with
ex: The road was slippery after the heavy rain.
大雨過後路面很滑。

en: n. a surface that goes up or down at an angle; the angle of such a surface; vi. to lean at an angle; to go up or down at an angle; vt. to make something lean or slant
ex: The ski slope was covered in fresh snow.
滑雪坡道上覆蓋著新雪。

en: n. a substance that is hard and keeps its shape; a. hard and firm; not hollow; strong and well built; made of the same material all the way through; (math) having length, width and height
ex: Water turns into a solid when it freezes.
水結冰時會變成固體。

en: adv. at some time in the future
ex: I hope to visit Japan someday.
我希望有一天能去日本。

en: adv. in a way that is not known or certain; for a reason that you do not understand
ex: I'll finish this project somehow, even if I have to stay up all night.
我一定會想辦法完成這個專案，就算得熬夜。

en: n. a type of pasta in the form of long thin strings, originally from Italy
ex: We had spaghetti with tomato sauce for dinner.
我們晚餐吃了番茄醬義大利麵。

en: a. clearly stated or defined; relating to one particular thing only; n. a particular detail or feature; a medicine that works well for a specific disease
ex: Could you be more specific about what you need?
你可以更具體地說明你需要什麼嗎？

en: n. a substance made from a plant that is added to food to give it flavor; excitement or interest; vt. to add spice to food; to make something more exciting
ex: Cinnamon is a spice often used in baking.
肉桂是一種經常用在烘焙的香料。

en: vt. to let a liquid flow over the edge of a container by accident; to make something fall; n. an amount of liquid that has spilled; a fall from a horse or bicycle
ex: Be careful not to spill your coffee on the carpet.
小心別把咖啡灑在地毯上。

en: vt. to make something turn around quickly; to make thread by twisting fibers; to tell a story that is not true; vi. to turn around and around quickly; n. a fast turning movement
ex: The dancer spun around on one foot.
舞者用一隻腳旋轉。

en: n. a plant with dark green leaves that are eaten as a vegetable; (slang) nonsense
ex: Popeye eats spinach to become strong.
大力水手吃菠菜變強壯。

en: n. a feeling of wanting to hurt or annoy someone; vt. to deliberately annoy someone
ex: She did it out of spite because she was jealous.
她出於嫉妒，惡意地那麼做。
ph: cut off one's nose to spite one's face

en: vi. to move through liquid so that drops fly about; (of liquid) to fly about in drops; n. the sound or movement of liquid hitting something; a bright mark or patch; a small amount
ex: The kids splashed in the pool all afternoon.
孩子們整個下午都在泳池裡濺水玩。

en: vt. to harm something so that it is no longer good; to treat a child too kindly so that it behaves badly; vi. (of food) to become bad; n. (plural) things taken from an enemy in war
ex: Don't let the bad weather spoil your trip.
別讓壞天氣毀了你的旅行。

en: n. a person who secretly collects information about another country or company; vt. to see or notice something; vi. to secretly watch someone
ex: The spy sent secret messages to his government.
那名間諜向他的政府發送秘密訊息。

en: vt. to press something firmly from the sides, especially to get liquid out; to push into a small space; vi. to press; n. an act of pressing something; a crowd where people are very close together
ex: She squeezed a lemon into her tea.
她把檸檬汁擠進茶裡。

en: a. no longer fresh, as in food that has become dry or bad; having lost interest or freshness; (of an idea) old and often used; n. urine of horses or cattle
ex: The bread was stale because it had been left out for days.
麵包放了好幾天，已經不新鮮了。

en: vi. to look at someone or something for a long time with the eyes wide open; vt. to look at someone steadily; n. a long steady look
ex: It's rude to stare at people on the train.
在火車上盯著別人看很沒禮貌。

en: v. to suffer or die because of lack of food; to make someone suffer or die from lack of food; (informal) to be very hungry
ex: Many people in the drought-hit area are starving.
受乾旱影響的地區有許多人正在挨餓。

en: a. firmly fixed and not likely to move; regular and continuous; calm and reliable; vt. to make something stable; vi. to become stable
ex: He has a steady job at the bank.
他在銀行有一份穩定的工作。

en: n. the hot gas that water changes into when it boils; energy or force; a. working by steam power; vi. to give off steam; to move by steam power; to get very angry
ex: Steam rose from the hot cup of tea.
熱茶杯裡冒出蒸氣。

en: a. rising or falling very quickly at a sharp angle; (of prices) too high; (of a change) very large and sudden; v. to soak something in liquid; n. a steep slope
ex: The path up the mountain was very steep.
通往山頂的小路非常陡峭。

en: a. made of or covered with a substance that sticks to things; (of weather) hot and uncomfortable; (informal) difficult or awkward
ex: My fingers were sticky from the honey.
我的手指因為蜂蜜而黏黏的。

en: n. a sharp pain caused by an insect or plant; a feeling of sharp hurt or pain; a sharp hurtful remark; vt. to hurt someone with a sharp point; to make someone feel upset; vi. to feel sharp pain
ex: A wasp stung him on the arm.
一隻黃蜂叮了他的手臂。
ph: 最後的刺激（意料之外的結局）
